name: Charles Shah
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember doing two salaries' worth of work on one pregnancy.” People around Juniper Street know Charles by a small Sunday habit. Charles knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I managed their books through both pregnancies. I want the years of unpaid work named before anyone divides the money.
appearance: Charles has iron-gray waves, a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, and a favorite piece of clothing, a plum-colored cardigan. It usually goes with one cuff folded back twice. When somebody else has the floor, Charles counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Charles is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
agenda: To record the years of unpaid work.
family: Charlie Emery is Charles’s half-sibling. Charles remembers the birthdays. Charlie asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The missing name on the stern*, Charlie says, “I ran the last voyage under that old spelling.”
connections: Ariel Jain. Unpaid parental work explains why the adult child sees inheriting the chair as an obligation.

reactions.situation: The divorcing founders ask staff to pick a side
reactions.response: Charles asks when the next wages will arrive before giving either founder a public endorsement.

reactions.situation: A witness is embarrassed about remembering only a little
reactions.response: Charles asks where they stood and what they could hear, leaving the rest open instead of filling it with guesses.

reactions.situation: If a relative arrives with a solution nobody requested
reactions.response: Charles thanks them for coming and explains the part that still belongs to the household.
